rv.q: The last thing the West End needs is an endless stream of American musicals, but this home-grown fare simply isn't good enough.
Otherwise, Terry Johnson's production, which cheeries up Stephen Frears's 2005 film, is thin fare.
Don Black's smart lyrics are beautifully framed by music reflecting the era including comic songs, romantic ballads and girl-group harmonies.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this WWII-era musical about London's Windmill Theatre, praising its period score and lead performances but questioning its old-fashioned approach and reliance on female nudity in a modern context.
